title: Check that the programs a bash script needs are installed before it runs
summary: Looks up each program your script depends on. If one is missing, the script tells you which ones to install and stops before doing any work.

steps.explain: Save the script. Create the file with nano and paste the whole text, including the first line that starts with #!. Press Ctrl+O then Enter to save, and Ctrl+X to exit.
steps.expect: An empty editor opens. After you save, the file exists in the current folder.

steps.explain: Check the script for syntax mistakes without running it.
steps.expect: No output means the syntax is correct.

steps.explain: Make the script executable so you can start it by its name.
steps.expect: No output. ls -l then shows x in the permissions.

steps.explain: Check three programs. tar and gzip are normally installed; nosuchtool42 is a made-up name that is not installed.
steps.cmd: ./<FILE> tar gzip nosuchtool42; echo exit code $?
steps.expect: found: tar, found: gzip, missing: nosuchtool42, install these before running the script: nosuchtool42, then exit code 1

steps.explain: Check only the programs that exist. The script reports that all dependencies were found.
steps.expect: found: tar (path), found: gzip (path), all dependencies found

warnings: command -v also finds aliases and shell functions. Check the exact program name that the script will run.
The check shows that a program exists, not that its version works or that it is the right program.
Put the check at the top of your script, so it stops before it changes any file.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-deps.sh - make sure the programs your script needs are installed.
# Usage: ./check-deps.sh PROGRAM [PROGRAM...]
# Prints each program as found or missing. Exit code: 0 when all are found, 1 when any is missing.

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# == 0 )); then
    echo "usage: $0 PROGRAM [PROGRAM...]" >&2
    exit 2
fi

missing=()
for prog in "$@"; do
    # command -v prints the path of a program that can be run. If it is not
    # found, it prints nothing and returns a non-zero exit code.
    if path=$(command -v "$prog"); then
        echo "found:   $prog ($path)"
    else
        echo "missing: $prog" >&2
        missing+=("$prog")
    fi
done

if (( ${#missing[@]} > 0 )); then
    echo "install these before running the script: ${missing[*]}" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "all dependencies found"

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer
